1.explanation: This minimal HTML page imports the Carbon CSS and renders two separate ordered lists using the `bx--list--ordered` class. In Firefox you will observe that the second list does not start at “1” as expected; it continues numbering from the first list. The nested example also demonstrates that nested lists still work, but the top‐level counter isn’t resetting between distinct <ol> elements. This shows the `counter-reset: item` rule in Carbon’s CSS is not behaving as a fresh reset in Firefox. Opening this file in Firefox reproduces the bug exactly as seen in the provided screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots illustrate that when using Carbon’s custom ordered‐list styles in Firefox, separate <ol> elements do not reset their numbers. In the Gatsby theme docs you can see one long list numbered 7–17, and if you split that into two <ol class="bx--list--ordered"> lists, the second list continues counting from the first (e.g. starts at 7). Attempts to override the counter‐reset via inline styles (counter-reset: none or unset) have no effect – the pseudo‐element numbering (counter(item)) still picks up where the last list left off. Removing the `counter-reset: item` rule entirely from Carbon’s stylesheet is the only way to restore native list‐reset behavior in Firefox.
